name: Reims 1938
notes: The Circuit de Reims-Gueux, a triangle of public roads laid out in 1926 west of Reims: the RN31 between Thillois and La Garenne, the D27 past the start line, and the road through the village of Gueux. 7.816 km of near-flat-out running with only the Thillois corner and the turn at Gueux to slow for, which made it one of the fastest circuits in Europe. The Grand Prix de la Marne ran here from 1926, and on 3 July 1938 the French Grand Prix went to Manfred von Brauchitsch's Mercedes-Benz W154 over 64 laps; Hermann Lang took pole at 2:39.2 and the fastest lap at 2:45.1. The village was bypassed for 1952, ending this layout. Converted from the rFactor original by F1PiloteJV.
